summary: Grants and HALT. New workbench/grants.py: grants as Kernel records (kas_grants, kas_grant_uses; forward-only migrations): an operation (a family such as 'edit files', a registry tool's key, or one Kernel operation), a target (a folder inside Files, or an object: a record, an App, a window) and a scope (this assignment, until a time in whole ms, always). grant.words (read) gives the plain words and their digest before approval; grant.give (approve) is refused unless the digest of the words you saw matches; grant.revoke (approve); grant.list (read). Enforced at dispatch in the Kernel's own path: K1's GRANT_CHECK for assignment.step (a change runs only when your press on that step covers it as shown, or a grant in force covers its operation and every target it resolves to), K2's GRANT_CHECK for tools.use, and a one-call permit that files_service.may_change and field.set's own save read. A grant authorises the proposed steps it covers (never what always asks, the model's pick alone, or what is marked for approval); a step outside every grant stops as 'needs your grant' (journal NEEDS_GRANT, nothing sent) with one press, 'Grant this for this assignment' (the grant for that step's exact target, then carry on). The model cannot create or widen one: approve scope only, digest of the shown words, grant.* never a step or a model plan choice (tool_selection.DENY), never given from inside her work. New workbench/halt_gate.py: HALT's own hold (setting kas.halt; halt.status read, halt.press/halt.release approve), apart from Stop all's work gate; press stops each running assignment through assignment.stop with HALT's words, holds every other open one with a HALTED journal line (what was done, what was only prepared), cancels her model's reply jobs, closes a running model turn (turns.request_for guards every request: no turn is sent while held, a running one is closed through its request's Stop), and runs registered stop hooks (STOP_HOOKS, for K6's sandboxes); release restarts nothing. K1 assignments obey both holds. An App's window wait (K2 apps.open) ends at once on HALT and the step is 'not verified', never done. halt.py uses it (plus her hand, AGENT-01's pause, the moment, her words); the HALT button and her column read HALT's own hold; her state word reads STOPPED while it holds. Stop all now spares any process in a session of its own or started through session_launch (the owner's program windows). Window: a GRANTS fold under ACTIVE WORK in her column (the grant asked for in plain words with its one press; else 'GRANTS [n] see them'), and a Grants page in the centre (waiting, in force with Revoke and uses, her own area, give a grant with the words shown before the press, ended). Smoke on a throwaway copy: 47 of 47 checks; frames in graphite, kasandra and day at 1920x1200 and graphite at 1366x768 (48 of 48 frame checks). Built, not tested in the owner's sense; nothing ran on the ThinkPad.

decisions: Authorisation and grants together: your press by name (or 'all') on a step covers exactly that step as it was shown (its planned, fixed targets); a grant record covers what it names; a change covered by neither stops 'needs your grant' at dispatch. A grant also authorises the proposed steps it covers, so routine work inside it does not ask again; K1's 'Authorise step n' keeps working as before. 'all' covers fixed targets only; a target that comes from an earlier step's output needs a grant.

The floor is never granted: what always asks (stacy_hand.ALWAYS_ASKS), the model's pick alone, approve-scope operations (by name only, as K1), reads (nothing to grant), sends (K2's send tools), desk acts (her hand follows the dial), her own controls and yours (assignment.*, grant.*, halt.*, ledger.*, jobs.*, remote.*, ...). Grants do not consult the dial: the dial is her hand in the window; assignments already waited for presses regardless of it.

Her own area (Files/Slate) stays hers by the Files rules: shown as a standing line on the Grants page, it covers a dispatch there (so K2's tools.use into Slate still works) but never authorises a step by itself.
'Grant this for this assignment' grants the step's operation on the file's folder (a folder target) or on the object, for that assignment only; then her column carries on (the action's 'then').

field.set saves through office.save, which is approve scope, so a field.set step could never finish under a step's bounded authority (a K1/K2 latent gap). With K3's one-call permit (a grant or your press on that very sheet), that one save is let through; nothing else is widened.

HALT stops running assignments first (journal: 'Stopped by you with HALT ... Step n was running when you pressed HALT'), then writes its hold, then holds the other open ones (state held, journal HALTED). A running step is stopped at its next safe point; nothing kills a process. Stop all still holds her assignments too (they obey both holds); HALT does not hold Graphite's jobs.

While HALT holds, turns.request_for gives no port (every ask answers from the desk, NOT_SENT 'STOPPED'); a request made before the press reads cancelled. Her model's reply jobs (local_brain.REPLY_TOOLS) are cancelled at the press.

Stop all spares every descendant in a session of its own (programs.* and the Apps start program windows that way) and any pid session_launch recorded; Graphite's own-session helpers are stopped by their own authority (jobs, workers, her model, consoles, debug tools) or end at their own limit (a confined run, a capture) - see findings.
The Grants page lives in the centre (open_destination 'grants'), reached from her column's GRANTS fold; no Settings-tree node was added, to stay clear of S5's Settings work beside me.
In a short column (1366x768) the grant card drops the assignment's title and the parenthetical so the six commands keep their row.

release_note: Grants and HALT. Kasandra changes nothing without your authority: a grant names what she may do, where (a folder or one object) and for how long (this assignment, until a time, always), you read it in plain words before your press, and the desk enforces it at every step; a step outside it stops as "needs your grant" with one press to grant it for that assignment. Grants are listed, with their uses, on the Grants page, each with Revoke. HALT, upper left, stops all of her managed work at once (assignments, her hand, her model's answers, her sandboxes), leaves each journal saying what was done and what was only prepared, and never touches the desktop, your apps or Graphite's own jobs; RESUME restarts nothing. Stop all now spares your program windows.
